plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub producing dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant four-lobed flowers. A beloved garden plant across temperate regions, it often peaks in the Northern Hemisphere in early to mid May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid spring to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Balkans in southeastern Europe; widely cultivated in North America, Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Lilac was the first plant to be named an official state flower in New Hampshire in 1919, and its fragrance comes from compounds that are used in perfumery.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces long, cascading racemes of pea-like, fragrant flowers before or as the leaves emerge. It twines counterclockwise and can cover pergolas and walls.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid spring to early summer (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China; cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the United States
plants.funFact: Some wisteria vines live for over a century; a Chinese Wisteria in Sierra Madre, California, planted in 1894 is considered one of the largest blossoming plants in the world, covering about an acre.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems. Late-flowering tulip varieties are at their peak in cooler northern regions such as the Netherlands, northern Europe, and northern parts of North America in early to mid May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (April to May; late varieties bloom in May)
plants.location: Originally from Central Asia and Turkey; cultivated worldwide, especially in the Netherlands, Canada, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: During the Dutch Golden Age in the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so valuable that a single bulb could cost more than a house, an episode known as Tulip Mania.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of petal-like bracts surrounding a central cone of true flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, it begins blooming as autumn turns toward winter, with flowering extending through spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through spring depending on the region; common blooms from March to November, with some blooming in May
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape in South Africa; also cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa and is adapted to survive wildfires, with underground lignotubers that resprout after burns.
